item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Again, might as well just copy-and-paste this at the front of each of my comments of yours: you're probably the best character writer on this site, and it shows in this piece. You managed to make all the different sects distinct and unique in a short period of time, which was well done, and the ending was perfectly executed as well (although the letter felt a bit Hallmark-schmaltzy).
Only complaints are small ones: the first letter didn't quite sound like it was written by a nine-year-old, foremost. Splitting hairs, but when you're going for such a distinctive voice such as that, accuracy is important. You probably could have made the schism feel more bitter as well. I was raised on one side of the Catholic/Protestant schism, and know many on the other side, and that is still something that people almost come to blows over. Obviously, you didn't have a lot of space to put 30 years of harsh religious debate into, and for the most part you did a fine job, but there could have been just a bit more to the emotional crux of it.
Overall, however, it's an excellent character piece, and reads about as believably as is possible for the subject matter. Very well done.

item.title: This Author Commentary is brought to you in part by the Broken Church.
item.content:encoded:
This was originally started out as something simple: just Robert Bumaro giving a sermon to adherents of his church, professing acceptance for the splinter churches. It eventually evolved into him actually meeting members of the other two churches, and… well, this happened.

There is a bit of an easter egg in this story, and I won't say what it is, but suffice to say, if you've read up to a certain point of a certain story arc on the site, something in this story will seem very familiar to you.
